challenges.name: udf-reducers-quiz
challenges.title: Read the Deliveries screen bugs
challenges.description: Three statements about the courier app's Deliveries screen before it moved to one state and one reducer. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: `state.value = state.value.copy(...)` is two steps: a read and a write. What can another coroutine do between them?
Count the boolean and nullable fields the old ViewModel had, and how many of their combinations the screen can draw sensibly.
StateFlow keeps one value. What happens to a value that is equal to the current one, or that is replaced before the UI collects it?

questions.question:
Two places update the screen state at the same time: the refresh coroutine and the filter chip handler.

```kotlin
class DeliveriesViewModel : ViewModel() {
    val state = MutableStateFlow(DeliveriesState())

    fun onFilter(filter: String) {
        state.value = state.value.copy(filter = filter)
    }

    private fun onLoaded(orders: List<Order>) {          // runs on Dispatchers.Default
        state.value = state.value.copy(orders = orders, refreshing = false)
    }
}
```

```text
14:02:11.180  onLoaded reads state (filter=all)
14:02:11.181  onFilter writes filter=picked
14:02:11.183  onLoaded writes orders=[...], filter=all
```

Statement: "StateFlow is thread-safe, so two writers that both use `state.value = state.value.copy(...)` cannot lose an update."
questions.explanation: False. Each assignment is atomic, but read-copy-write is two operations: `onLoaded` read the state before `onFilter` wrote, then wrote its copy with the old filter, so the courier's chip choice vanished. `MutableStateFlow.update { reduce(it, action) }` retries the function until a compare-and-set succeeds, so concurrent updates are applied one after the other. Keeping the `MutableStateFlow` private and exposing `asStateFlow()` also stops the screen from writing it directly.

questions.question:
The old ViewModel kept six independent fields:

```kotlin
val isLoading = MutableLiveData(false)
val isRefreshing = MutableLiveData(false)
val error = MutableLiveData<String?>(null)
val orders = MutableLiveData<List<Order>>(emptyList())
val filter = MutableLiveData("all")
val banner = MutableLiveData<String?>(null)
```

```text
Bug RR-412: after a failed pull-to-refresh the spinner keeps turning,
and the next successful load shows fresh orders under the old "timeout" banner.
```

Statement: "Six independent fields allow combinations the screen should never show; one immutable state class changed only by a reducer makes every transition explicit and testable as a plain function."
questions.explanation: True. Nine call sites each set some of the six fields, and the bug is two missed writes: refreshing was never reset on failure, and error was never cleared on success. With one `data class` and a pure `reduce(state, action)`, each action lists every field it changes in one place, and a unit test can feed actions and compare states without Android, coroutines or mocks.

questions.question:
The team wanted a toast for every pickup and put a counter in the state:

```kotlin
data class DeliveriesState(/* ... */ val lastPickedUp: String? = null)

// screen
val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
LaunchedEffect(state.lastPickedUp) {
    state.lastPickedUp?.let { toast("Picked up $it") }
}
```

```text
Courier picks up O7, then O7 again after an undo: one toast.
Two pickups 5 ms apart (O7, O8): one toast, for O8.
```

Statement: "StateFlow keeps only the latest value and does not emit a value equal to the current one, so a UI that must react to every occurrence cannot rely on a plain state field like this."
questions.explanation: True. StateFlow is conflated and distinct-until-changed: setting the same value again emits nothing, and a value replaced before the collector runs is never seen. State describes what the screen shows now; things that must happen once each (a toast, a navigation) need either a list of pending messages that the UI acknowledges, or a channel. Lesson 3 covers both.

challenges.name: deliveries-reducer
challenges.title: Write the Deliveries reducer
challenges.description: The courier app's Deliveries screen moves to unidirectional data flow: one `DeliveriesState`, one `sealed interface Action`, and a pure `reduce(state, action)` that `DeliveriesViewModel` calls inside `state.update { }`. The editor holds the file with each branch of the reducer missing, marked by a `// [ ]` line; until every branch is in place the compiler reports that `when` is not exhaustive. Some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: the first load shows the spinner and clears an old error; pull-to-refresh keeps the current list on screen; fresh orders replace the list and clear spinner, refresh and error; a failed request stops both spinners and shows the message while keeping the last list; a filter chip only changes the filter; picking up an order changes that order's status and nothing else. Run feeds actions to `reduce` and prints what the screen would show after each one.
hints: For each action, list every field the screen reads (spinner, refreshing, error, list, filter) and decide whether this action must change it. A forgotten field is the classic bug.
Every branch returns `state.copy(...)` with the fields it changes; lists are replaced, never mutated (`map` returns a new list).

A reducer for a chat screen: `is Action.Send -> state.copy(sending = true, error = null)`, `is Action.Sent -> state.copy(messages = state.messages + action.message, sending = false)`, `is Action.SendFailed -> state.copy(sending = false, error = action.reason)`, `is Action.Edit -> state.copy(messages = state.messages.map { if (it.id == action.id) it.copy(text = action.text) else it })`.
